Smart Reads of the Week: Singapore Bank Stocks, Temasek Share Buybacks, REIT Dividends, and AI Risks
article:
Singapore stocks are finding their footing after last week’s sharp sell-off, when the STI fell 4.1%, led by weakness in bank shares. Meanwhile, concerns over the debt financing the AI boom have unsettled global technology markets.
For investors, these developments raise a familiar question: when share prices fall, are we looking at a buying opportunity or a warning sign?
This week’s Smart Reads explores that question through Singapore’s three major banks. After their recent pullback, we examine whether DBS, OCBC and UOB have become attractive enough to buy, or whether investors should remain patient.
We also look at four Temasek-linked companies aggressively buying back their shares, and three REITs offering yields above 6%. Both may appeal to income investors, but attractive shareholder returns are only meaningful when the underlying businesses can support them.
Elsewhere, the potential deal between StarHub and Keppel involving M1 could reshape Singapore’s telecommunications industry, while the upcoming Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link raises fresh questions for Frasers Centrepoint Trust.
And for long-term investors, we revisit what a S$10,000 investment in iFAST a decade ago would be worth today, alongside a closer look at whether the AI boom’s growing reliance on debt should be a cause for concern.
Here are this week’s top articles:
Top 4 Temasek-Linked Stocks Aggressively Buying Back Their Shares
These Temasek-linked companies are repurchasing their shares, but what do these buybacks really mean for long-term shareholders?
Singapore Bank Shares Have Fallen. Are They Cheap Enough Yet?
DBS, OCBC and UOB have pulled back from their highs. We examine whether their valuations now offer better buying opportunities.
Get Smart: One Lot of DBS For S$14,000?
Smaller SGX board lots make expensive blue chips more accessible, but the real advantage is greater control over your portfolio.
StarHub and Keppel Shares: What the Potential M1 Deal Means for Investors
A potential deal involving M1 could reshape Singapore’s telecommunications industry. We examine what it could mean for both companies.
3 REITs Paying More Than 6%: Are Their Dividends Safe?
Yields above 6% may look tempting, but investors should examine whether the underlying cash flows can sustain those distributions.
The RTS Link Countdown: Is Frasers Centrepoint Trust Built to Withstand the S$290M Retail Drain?
The upcoming RTS Link could shift more spending towards Johor Bahru. Can FCT’s suburban malls withstand the potential impact?
If You Invested S$10,000 in iFAST 10 Years Ago, Here’s How Much You’d Have Today
We look back at iFAST’s decade-long journey to see how patient shareholders have been rewarded.
The AI Boom Is Being Built on Debt: Should Investors Be Worried?
AI investment continues to accelerate, but growing reliance on debt raises important questions about financial sustainability and future returns.
